names.official: Tax withheld on wages and salaries
names.native: Impôt retenu sur les traitements et salaires

taxes.base: Wages and salaries; withheld each month by the employer using the tax tables.

rate.headline: 0% to 42% progressive
details: The scale rises from 8% on taxable income above EUR 13,230 to 42% above EUR 234,870, after the 2025 indexation of 2.5 brackets (PwC).
Rate as summarised by PwC (review of July–August 2026), not checked against the Luxembourg tax administrations.

instruments.explanation: The largest direct tax. Luxembourg also collects a solidarity surcharge on top (next row). All of it is a State tax; communes receive none of it in the national accounts.

names.official: Personal income tax fixed by assessment
names.native: Impôt sur le revenu des personnes physiques fixé par voie d’assiette

taxes.base: Income that is assessed after a tax return: self-employment, rents, and other income not taxed by withholding.

rate.headline: Same progressive scale as the wage tax
details: Rate as summarised by PwC (review of July–August 2026), not checked against the Luxembourg tax administrations.

instruments.explanation: Assessed on the same scale as wages.

names.official: Solidarity surcharge on personal income tax
names.native: Impôt de solidarité (majoration) des personnes physiques

taxes.base: A surcharge calculated on the income tax of individuals.

rate.headline: A percentage added to the income tax
details: The National Tax List calls it "Supplementary solidarity income tax"; the rate is not itemised there.

instruments.explanation: The surcharge brings in EUR 608 million in 2024.

names.official: Withholding taxes on capital income, directors’ fees and interest, and smaller withholding taxes
names.native: Impôt retenu sur les revenus de capitaux; tantièmes; retenue libératoire sur les intérêts

taxes.base: Dividends and other capital income (EUR 1,053 million), directors’ fees (EUR 74 million), interest of residents (EUR 171 million, final withholding), certain income of non-residents (EUR 1 million), contributions to a supplementary pension plan for the self-employed (EUR 6 million) and a temporary balancing tax (EUR 0.01 million).
taxes.payer: Recipients of the income; the payer withholds.

instruments.explanation: Six lines of the National Tax List that tax investment income at source.

legalRefs.locator: sheet LU, D51A C02, C05, C06, C08, C10, C11

names.official: Corporation tax, its solidarity surcharge and the real estate levy
names.native: Impôt sur le revenu des collectivités; impôt de solidarité; prélèvement immobilier

taxes.base: Taxable profit of companies; the surcharge (EUR 262 million) is added to the tax; the real estate levy is EUR 8 million.

rate.headline: 15% to EUR 175,000 of income; 17% above EUR 200,000
details: Plus a solidarity surtax of 7% of the tax; the overall rate with the municipal business tax is 24.94% in Luxembourg City (PwC).
Rate as summarised by PwC (review of July–August 2026), not checked against the Luxembourg tax administrations.

instruments.explanation: The State’s corporate income tax. The municipal business tax (trade tax) is drawn under the communes.

names.official: Net wealth tax
names.native: Impôt sur la fortune

taxes.base: The net assets of companies (since 2006 the tax no longer applies to individuals).

rate.headline: Set by law
details: The National Tax List shows EUR 1,101.5 million in 2024, about the same as in 2023.

instruments.explanation: A significant revenue source for Luxembourg.

names.official: Subscription tax on company securities ("holding tax")
names.native: Taxe d’abonnement sur les titres de société

taxes.base: As named in the National Tax List: company securities, booked as a tax on production.

rate.headline: Set by the Law on the taxe d’abonnement
details: EUR 1,317.3 million in 2024 and EUR 1,216.7 million in 2023.

instruments.explanation: The fourth largest tax line in the State’s list.

names.official: Inheritance duty
names.native: Droits de succession

taxes.base: Inheritances other than those in direct line.

instruments.explanation: EUR 134 million in 2024.

names.official: Value added tax
names.native: Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée

taxes.base: Goods and services supplied in Luxembourg and imports.
taxes.payer: Consumers; businesses charge it and claim input credits.

rate.headline: 17% standard; 14%, 8% and 3% reduced
details: The standard rate of 17% is the lowest in the EU; 14% on certain wines and advertising pamphlets; 8% on gas and electricity; 3% on food, books, pharmaceuticals and children’s clothing (PwC).
The pre-2023 rates were reinstated on 1 January 2024 after a temporary one-point cut in 2023 (Luxembourg Chronicle).
Rate as summarised by PwC (review of July–August 2026), not checked against the Luxembourg tax administrations.

instruments.explanation: The second largest tax line after the wage tax.
exceptions: Banking, financial and insurance services are generally exempt.

names.official: Import duties and levies on imported agricultural products
names.native: Droits sur les importations; prélèvements agricoles

taxes.base: Goods imported from outside the EU, by the Common Customs Tariff.

rate.headline: EU Common Customs Tariff
details: An EU own resource; Eurostat records it under the EU institutions.

instruments.explanation: Collected for the EU budget.

names.official: Excise duty on tobacco (on imports and on national production)
names.native: Droits d’accise sur le tabac

taxes.base: Cigarettes and other tobacco products.
taxes.payer: Producers and importers; passed on in the price.

rate.headline: Fixed by law
details: EUR 1,152.3 million is booked as excise on imports of tobacco and EUR 103.5 million on national production in 2024.

instruments.explanation: The excise on imports of tobacco is the larger part of the line.

legalRefs.locator: sheet LU, D2122C C08, D214A C04

names.official: Excise duties on mineral oils and gases, the supplementary fuel tax and the CO₂ tax
names.native: Droits d’accise sur les huiles minérales; taxe complémentaire; taxe CO₂

taxes.base: Petrol, diesel and heating oil by volume; liquefied gas; the CO₂ tax on fuels (EUR 228 million) and on gas (EUR 29 million).
taxes.payer: Fuel importers and suppliers; passed on at the pump.

rate.headline: Per litre or per tonne, fixed by law
details: EUR 387 million excise on mineral oils, EUR 150 million autonomous excise, EUR 115 million supplementary tax, EUR 228 million CO₂ tax (fuels) and EUR 29 million CO₂ tax (gas) in 2024.

instruments.explanation: Seven lines that tax energy products.

legalRefs.locator: sheet LU, D2122C C02 to C06 and C16, D214L C06

names.official: Excise duties and consumption tax on alcoholic beverages, beer and intermediate products
names.native: Droits d’accises et taxe de consommation sur les alcools

taxes.base: Alcoholic beverages, imported and nationally produced.
taxes.payer: Producers and importers; passed on in the price.

instruments.explanation: Eight small lines of the list, together EUR 76 million.

legalRefs.locator: sheet LU, D2122C C01, C07, C09, C10, C14, D214A C01 to C03

names.official: Taxes on electricity, natural gas and water
names.native: Taxes sur l’électricité, le gaz naturel et le prélèvement d’eau

taxes.base: Electricity (supplementary tax, distribution and production taxes), natural gas consumption and water abstraction.

rate.headline: Set by law
details: EUR 13.4 million water, 4.6 million production of electricity, 3.9 million natural gas, 1.7 million supplementary electricity tax and 1.2 million electricity distribution in 2024.

instruments.explanation: Five lines.

legalRefs.locator: sheet LU, D214L C01 to C05

names.official: Insurance premiums tax and the special tax in aid of the rescue service
names.native: Taxe sur les assurances; impôt spécial en charge des assureurs

taxes.base: Insurance premiums; the special tax is borne by insurers for the rescue service.

instruments.explanation: A small tax on insurance contracts.

names.official: Registration duties, mortgage duties and the mortgage duty on salaries
names.native: Droits d’enregistrement; droits d’hypothèques

taxes.base: Deeds and transfers of immovable property, and mortgages.

rate.headline: Set by law
details: The communes receive a surtax on property transfers, drawn in their part. Registration duties fell from EUR 233.8 million in 2023 to EUR 170.3 million in 2024.

instruments.explanation: The State’s taxes on property transactions.

legalRefs.locator: sheet LU, D214C C02 to C04

names.official: Vehicle registration and motor vehicle taxes (enterprises and households) and ship taxes
names.native: Taxe d’immatriculation; taxe sur véhicules automoteurs; taxe sur les navires

taxes.base: The registration and ownership of motor vehicles and boats.

rate.headline: By engine and emissions
details: EUR 41.0 million paid by households and EUR 27.9 million by enterprises on motor vehicles; EUR 10.2 million registration; EUR 0.9 million ships and boats.

instruments.explanation: Five lines.

legalRefs.locator: sheet LU, D214D C01, D29B C01 and C02, D59F C05 and C06

names.official: Contributions to the Deposit Guarantee Fund (FGDL) and the Resolution Fund (FRL)
names.native: Contributions au FGDL et au FRL

taxes.base: As named in the National Tax List; no further detail.

rate.headline: Set by the funds
details: The Resolution Fund line fell from EUR 243.4 million in 2023 to EUR 0.07 million in 2024.

instruments.explanation: Compulsory contributions that the statisticians book as taxes on production.

legalRefs.locator: sheet LU, D29H C05 and C06

names.official: Casino levy (State part), stamp duties, chancellery fees, dog tax and others
names.native: Prélèvements sur les jeux de casino; droits de timbre; timbres de chancellerie; taxe sur les chiens

taxes.base: Casino gambling (EUR 20.1 million), stamp duties (10.6), fees concerning foreign affairs (6.5), dog tax (1.5), chancellery stamps (1.0) and reclassified VAT (2.2).

instruments.explanation: The smaller State lines of the list.

legalRefs.locator: sheet LU, D214F C01, D29H C04, D59F C01 to C04

names.official: Employers’ actual social contributions
names.native: Cotisations sociales des employeurs

taxes.base: Gross pay. The National Tax List gives it as a subtotal split into pension (EUR 2,404 million) and non-pension (EUR 1,369 million) contributions.

rate.headline: Set by the Social Security Code
details: Employee contributions are listed by PwC (sickness 2.80%, pension 8%); the employer’s rates are not extracted here.

instruments.explanation: The list does not itemise below the subtotal.

names.official: Compulsory social contributions of employees
names.native: Cotisations sociales des salariés

taxes.base: Gross pay up to a monthly ceiling.

rate.headline: Sickness 2.80% and pension 8% of gross pay, among others
details: PwC lists 2.80% for sickness and 8% for pension, each limited to a monthly ceiling of EUR 13,518.68 from May 2025, and a dependency contribution on gross income.
Rate as summarised by PwC (review of July–August 2026), not checked against the Luxembourg tax administrations.

instruments.explanation: The largest social contribution line.

names.official: Contributions of the non-employed, the self-employed and voluntary contributions
names.native: Cotisations des non-salariés, des indépendants et volontaires

taxes.base: As labelled in the National Tax List: compulsory contributions by the non-employed (EUR 1,227 million), by the self-employed (EUR 4 million) and voluntary households’ contributions (EUR 72 million).

rate.headline: Set by the Social Security Code

instruments.explanation: The remaining households’ contributions.

names.official: Municipal business (trade) tax
names.native: Impôt commercial communal

taxes.base: Business profit of companies and of self-employed people, calculated like the State tax and then multiplied by a municipal rate.

rate.headline: About 6.75% in Luxembourg City
details: The rate varies by commune; PwC gives 6.75% in Luxembourg City, which with the corporation tax and the surtax makes 24.94%.
Rate as summarised by PwC (review of July–August 2026), not checked against the Luxembourg tax administrations.

instruments.explanation: The communes’ main tax: EUR 1.63 billion, 96% of their taxes in the list.

names.official: Property tax (land and buildings), tax on secondary residences and tax on land without buildings
names.native: Impôt foncier; taxe sur les résidences secondaires

taxes.base: Land and buildings by assessed value; secondary residences.

rate.headline: A municipal multiplier on a State base
details: The list does not give rates.

instruments.explanation: Small in Luxembourg: EUR 45.6 million.

legalRefs.locator: sheet LU, D29A C01 and C02, D59A C02

names.official: Surtax on property transfers, casino levy (communal part), tourist tax, construction tax in dense sectors, cabaret and entertainment taxes
names.native: Surtaxe sur les mutations immobilières; taxe de séjour; taxe sur les amusements publics

taxes.base: Property transfers (EUR 6.9 million), casinos (5.2), tourist stays (3.8), construction in dense sectors (2.0), licensed premises (0.5) and public entertainment (0.9).

rate.headline: Set by law and by commune

instruments.explanation: Six small lines that Eurostat’s accounts place with local government.

legalRefs.locator: sheet LU, D214C C01, D214E, D214F C02, D214H
